arguments.task: Review uncommitted working tree changes to the frontend RequestHandler and its functional test before they are pushed to Gerrit

outcomes.evidence: The first calls were typo3_project_describe, git diff and git status, then typo3_task_guide with the two changed paths and changeType audit; the rule lookups, the changelog lookups by tag and the documentation lookup came after the diff was read. The answer opens with the tree at 088d17cc272 on main, the target 15.0, the subsystem (frontend RequestHandler::generateHtmlTag()) and the functional test beside it.

1.1 ties RequestHandler.php:867-870 to the breaking-change rule from core/contribution/commit-messages and names the consequence: a site with htmlTag_setParams = none silently gets lang back, htmlTag_stdWrap has no replacement. 2.1 names tsref.xml:341 and :376-385 and typoscript.ts:459 against the precedent commit d08605405ab; 2.2 names :854 and the deleted test case that pinned the old semantics. Spot-checked in the checkout: all three lines and the precedent commit exist.

It ran runTests.sh -s functional -d sqlite -- RequestHandlerTest.php first (20 tests OK), then cgl -n, checkIntegrityPhp and phpstan, and §4 names by suite what it did not run: full functional, unit, checkRst, checkExtensionScannerRst, build, e2e, with the reason for each.

Commit shape is marked not applicable yet because nothing is committed, the changelog and the documentation follow-up are raised because the diff removes two documented TypoScript options and adds one, and public PHP API is checked and found unchanged. Security gets one line at the escaping the diff touches and nothing beyond it.

Four tiers, blocks submission first, then what a reviewer sends back, then worth a change, then checked and found correct, with raised-and-dropped at the end. git status after the run is identical to before; the two untracked helper files were copied into the session's own scratchpad outside the checkout and compared, not moved.

failures.evidence: Every finding carries a line of the diff or of the checkout, and §4 reports what the code does from reading :832-871 against the caller :353-404, not from what RequestHandler used to do.

The checks are the ones the diff touches: the breaking-change rule, the changelog entry, the tsref and the parser keyword list. The two changelog lookups by tag TypoScript were the widest calls, and the answer used them for the deprecate-first precedents alone rather than as a checklist.

Core conventions applied to a core patch: [!!!] before the keyword, a Breaking and a Feature RST on one issue, Releases: main only because a breaking change reaches no release line. No extension or site rule appears.
git status before and after the run are byte-identical; the only write went to /tmp under the session's own scratchpad. The suites it ran are the dry ones, cgl with -n included.
